q: “Life among the stars. Pretty amazing stuff, huh, captain?” “Yeppers, boss.”
2006 August 6, Jackson Publick, “Twenty Years to Midnight” (22:01 from the start), in The Venture Bros., season 2, episode 5, spoken by Pirate Captain (Christopher McCulloch):

“He told you?”
“He said you shot a bucket.”
“Shit.”
“Hey, don't beat yourself over it! Oops! Freudian slip. Sorry. Listen up, bro, all the guys will jack this trip. It's either that or wet dreamland.”
“You too?” he asked, surprised and hopeful.
“Yeppo.”

e: Representing yeah pronounced with the mouth snapped closed at the end (yeah + -p). Compare yup and nope. Compare also German jap (“yep”).

q: Bingo, I thought. Hoho haha, yep yeppity yes.

Yeppity, sir. You're exactly the kind of lucky guy who does OK by this plan.
2007 November 2, Mark Lane, “Another tax plan, more FAQ”, in The Daytona Beach News-Journal:

“But it says five—whoa. You mean five hundred thousand?“
“Yeppity."
2011, Caprice Crane, With a Little Luck, Bantam Books, →ISBN, page 272:

e: From Middle English ȝeply, ȝapliche, ȝepliche, from Old English ġēaplīċe (“cleverly; cunningly; deceitfully; boldly”), equivalent to yep + -ly.

q: "Yepper," said Cheryl. She could tell from Peter's reaction that the whole story was true.

e: From Middle English yespon, yepson, ȝespon, ȝespen, ȝispon (“a measure of volume equivalent to that contained in a person’s hands cupped together”), probably from Old English *ġēapsponn, *ġēapspann, from Old English *ġēap (“bent, curved”) + spann (“measure of the palm or hand”), equivalent to gap + span. Compare West Frisian gasp (“buckle, clasp”), Dutch gesp (“buckle, clasp”), Middle Low German gespe (“the cavity between the hands when held together”), Old Norse gaupn (“hollow made by cupped hands”). Doublet of gowpen.
